In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah al-Kadh (al-Inshiqaq)

It is Meccan, and Allah knows best.

The saying of Allah Most High: ﴿When the sky is split asunder﴾ has the same meaning as His saying: ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾. It is also said: it is split open with the clouds, like His saying: ﴿And the Day the sky will be split open with clouds﴾, which we have already mentioned. And it is said: it is split open for the descent of the angels.

In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: it is split open for the descent of the Lord, exalted is His name, and that is without how (bila kayf). And it is said: (it is torn apart).

And from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: the sky will be split from the Milky Way. And it is said: it is the gate of the sky.

Its saying: ﴿And it has listened to its Lord and it is right that it should⁠﴾ means: it listened to the command of its Lord, and it is right for it to listen.

The poet says:

(The heart has been distracted by Baddan... indeed my concern is with listening and hearing.)

And some of them said: "They are deaf when they hear good that is mentioned about them, and when evil is mentioned about them, they listen (adhanu), i.e., they listened (istama'u)."

And in the report from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has never given ear (adhina) to anything as He gives ear to a Prophet who chants the Qur'an beautifully."

As for the hearing of the heaven, it is possible that it is literal, and it is possible that its hearing is its submission to what it is commanded, and Allah knows best.

And His words: ﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾, meaning: it is stretched out like a hide (leather), so that no mountain or anything else remains upon it, except that it enters into its interior. It is also said: its extent is increased so that it may accommodate them.

It is related from some of them: it is changed from its form by alteration and otherwise, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿stretched out﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And it casts out what is within it and empties itself﴾ — meaning: it casts out what is in its belly, of treasures and the dead, so that its belly is emptied. It is also said: it casts out what it was entrusted with, and empties itself of what it was made to keep. It is as if it casts off what is upon its back and empties itself of what is in its belly.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 84, verse 5:

And His saying: ﴿And it has listened to its Lord and has been made to comply﴾ — we have already explained it.

If it is said: Where is the response (jawab) to His saying ﴿When the sky splits open﴾, when it requires a response? The answer comes in several ways. Al-Farra' said: its response is omitted, and the meaning is: "When the sky splits open and such-and-such occurs, every person will see what he has found of reward and punishment." And it is said: every denier of the resurrection will know that he was in error and misguidance.

The second way: the response is His saying ﴿And it has listened﴾, and the waw is extra (za'idah), so the response is: "it has listened."

The third way: the response is His saying ﴿then you will meet it﴾ (fa-mulaqihi), meaning: he will meet his deeds, good and bad.

The fourth way: in the verse there is an inversion of order (taqdim wa ta'khir), and the meaning is: "O mankind, indeed you are labouring toward your Lord with toil, so you will meet it when the sky splits open."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 84, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, indeed you are working your way toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾. Qatadah said: "Working for your Lord, working deeds."

Al-kadh (toil) is striving with exertion and fatigue.

The poet said:

(The brightness of every good life has passed away... and I remain toiling and exhausting myself for living.)

It is also permissible that the mention of the singular here carries the meaning of the plural, so it means: "O people."

Al-Hasan al-Basri used to say: "O man," and all of you are that man.

.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and you will meet Him﴾, Qatadah said: that is, you will meet your deeds, of good and of evil.

And it is said: "You will meet your Lord."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 84, verses 7–8:

And His saying: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to a light account﴾.

That is, an easy reckoning. It has been said concerning "easy" (yasir) that it means that good deeds are accepted and bad deeds are overlooked.

It is also established, by the narration of Abu Malikah from ʿĀʾishah, that the Prophet said: "Whoever is scrutinised in his reckoning will be destroyed." I said: "O Messenger of God, but God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to a light account﴾." He said: "That is merely the presentation (al-ʿarḍ)." May Allah be pleased with him. Abu al-Husayn Ibn al-Naqur informed us of this hadith; Abu Tahir (Ibn) al-Mukhlis informed us; Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us; al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Marwazi informed us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from ʿUthman ibn al-Aswad, from Ibn Abi Malikah, the report.

Abu ʿIsa (al-Tirmidhi) also cited, by the narration of Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet said: "Whoever is called to account will be punished," and it is with a gharib (unusual) chain.

In a third narration from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet saw her raising her hands while saying: "O Allah, reckon with me with an easy reckoning."

He said: "O ʿĀʾishah, do you know what that reckoning is?" ʿĀʾishah said: "I said: God mentioned it in His Book: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to a light account﴾." The Messenger of God said: "Whoever is reckoned with is ruined; that is only the presentation before God, the Exalted."

Al-Hakim Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Hafiz mentioned in al-Mustadrak ʿala al-Sahihayn, with its chain, from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said: "Whoever has three qualities, God will reckon with him with an easy reckoning, and will admit him to Paradise by His mercy."

Abu Hurayrah said: "I said: O Messenger of God, for whom is this?" He said: "That you join the one who cuts you off, pardon the one who wrongs you, and give to the one who withholds from you."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 84, verse 9–10:

And His saying: ﴿And he will return to his people, delighted.﴾ That is: joyful and rejoicing. It is also permissible that he returns to his people from among the wide-eyed maidens (al-huur al-'iin), and it is also permissible that the meaning is: he returns to his people who were with him in the world. It was said: it was revealed concerning Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Asad, who was the husband of Umm Salama, and he was the first to emigrate (hijra) to Madina.

And His saying: ﴿But as for him who is given his record behind his back﴾ it was revealed concerning al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Asad.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿But as for him who is given his record behind his back﴾. Mujahid said: he dislocates his right hand and places his left hand behind his back, and his record is placed in it.

Al-Kalbi said: his right hand is shackled, and his record is placed in his left hand from behind his back.

Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, whose name is 'Abd Allah ibn Qays, narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection there will be three occasions of presentation (ʿardat): two of them are for disputation and excuses, and the third occasion is at the flying of the scrolls (tatayyur al-suhuf), so one will take [his record] in his right hand and take [it] in his left."

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir, with his chain of narration, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes account of himself in the world, Allah will make the reckoning easy for him in the Hereafter."

﴿So he will call out for destruction (thubur)﴾. Its meaning: he will say, "Woe to me for destruction!" (wa-thubūrāh), and the meaning of his saying "wa-thubūrāh" is: "Woe to me for ruin!" (wa-ihlākāh).

It is said: a man who is mathbūr means: one who is destroyed (hālik).

And His saying: ﴿And burn in a Blaze﴾, meaning: he will endure the Fire. It is also said: he will enter it. From this is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Burn therein﴾, meaning: enter it. It was also recited, "wa-yuṣallā saʿīran" (and he will be made to burn in a blaze), meaning: His punishment with the Fire of Hell will be intensified. This was related by al-Azharī.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 84, verse 13:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, he used to be joyful among his people﴾. That is: he did not grieve over falling short in the commands of Allah, nor did he tire or toil in acting in obedience to Allah. This was related by al-Qaffal.

It is also said: "he used to be joyful among his people," that is: riding his desire and following his appetite.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 84, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, he thought that he would never return﴾, meaning: that he would never return to Allah, the Exalted. This is a report of his denial of the Resurrection.

And His saying: ﴿yahur﴾ means yarji'u (he would return). From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I seek refuge in Allah from al-hawr after al-kawr," meaning: from decline after increase.

In another narration: "from al-hawr after al-kawr," meaning: from the dispersal of one's affair after it had been united, or from the corruption of one's affair after it had been good.

.

The poet said:

(And a man is nothing but like a meteor and its light; it turns to ash after it was blazing.)
"And His saying: ﴿Yes! Indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him﴾ means: knowing."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 84, verse 16:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So I swear by the twilight﴾, meaning: I swear by the twilight. Mujahid said: it is the whole of the day.

What is well known is that the shafaq (twilight) is the redness from the setting of the sun until the late evening prayer (al-'isha').

Al-Farra' said: I heard the Arabs say, "On so-and-so is a garment as if it were the shafaq," and he had on him a garment dyed with redness.

In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is related that he said: "The shafaq is the redness."

This is the view of a group of the Companions and a group of the Followers, among them Ibn 'Umar, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and others.

And it is related from Abu Hurayrah that the shafaq is the whiteness, and this is the view of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz.

And the night and what it gathers together (﴿وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ﴾).

That is: and what it gathers and wraps up, and brings together things after they have spread out. He said this because when night comes, it draws every thing back to its shelter, and every person returns to his home; whereas when day comes, they spread out to go about their affairs.

And His saying: ﴿And by the moon when it becomes full﴾ — that is, when its light gathers together. It is also said: it becomes full of light, and this is on the thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth nights of the month.

.

The poet said:

(Indeed we have she-camels, young and sturdy, ... gathered together, [if only] they found a driver.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 84, verse 19:

And His saying: ﴿You will surely embark on stage after stage.﴾ It is also read "لتركبن" (latarkabanna) in the singular. As for whoever reads it in the plural, its meaning is: "You will surely embark, O people, state after state." The word "ḥāl" (state) has the same meaning as "ṭabaq" (stage, layer).

The poet says:

(While a man is in a pleasant, luxurious, soft life, a decline comes upon him one day, on a slippery turning.)

The meaning of "state after state" is that he becomes a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a lump of flesh (muḍgha), then the spirit is breathed into him. After that his conditions change and vary from the familiar known stages of childhood, youth, old age, and other than these.

It is also said: "You will surely embark stage after stage" means: hardship upon hardship. The meaning is: life, then death, then resurrection, then recompense.

As for the reading in the singular, there are two opinions concerning it.

The first: what is meant is the sky, and the meaning is that it will split and become at one time like red oil (dihān), at another like molten metal (muhl), at another split open, and at another intact. This is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and others.

The second opinion: it is an address to the Prophet, and the meaning is: "You will surely embark upon the layers of the heavens, layer upon layer," and that was on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey). It is also said: "You will surely embark stage after stage" means: the loins of the fathers (aṣlāb al-ābāʾ), and that refers to the Messenger.

Al-ʿAbbas said in praise of the Prophet:

(Before it, you were pure in the loins, and in a repository when the leaves were being stitched together.)

(You moved from loin to womb, and whenever a world passed away, a layer appeared.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 84, verses 20–21:

And His saying ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe? And when the Quran is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ In the tafsir (explanation) it is said: the Prophet prostrated, and his companions with him, while the disbelievers stood over their heads clapping and whistling. So Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe? And when the Quran is recited to them, they do not prostrate?﴾ And it has been established through the narration of Abu Hurayrah that "the Prophet prostrated in this place."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 84, verse 24:

His saying: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ means: I make the Fire, in place of the good tidings given to the believers of Paradise, their portion.

Wa qawluhu: ﴿Illa alladhina amanu wa 'amilu as-salihat lahum ajrun ghayru mamnun﴾ ayy ghayru manqus wa la maqtu'.

Wa yuqal: la yamunnu 'alayhim ahadun ghayru Allah ta'ala fayukaddiruhu 'alayhim al-minna, wallahu a'lam.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds; theirs is a reward never to be cut off.﴾ That is, not diminished and not interrupted.

It is also said: no one bestows a favour upon them except Allah the Exalted, so that the obligation of favour would not spoil it for them. And Allah knows best.
